review_unsupported_claims: The rationale says the bank 'defined documents for income confirmation' and the evidence calls §5.1 and §5.2 'partial'. They address income proof but not the no-model route; §5.2 allows a declaration alone, which sits badly with the duty to establish the business area and income volume.
review_comment: The regulation requires, without a data model, that the lender 'უნდა დაადგინოს მსესხებლის საქმიანობის სფერო და შემოსავლის მოცულობა', but §5.2 says 'საკმარისია მსესხებლის დეკლარაცია; დამატებითი დოკუმენტი ან ბანკის შიდა მეთოდოლოგიით შემოწმება არ მოითხოვება' for loans up to 10 000 GEL, which conflicts rather than merely omits. The proposal appends the duty to §5.1 but leaves §5.2 untouched, so the conflict stays.

The regulation asks the lender to request income records 'და უზრუნველყოს ასლების შენახვა'. Neither §5.1 nor §5.2 mentions requesting income records or keeping copies, so 'partial' overstates what §5.1 covers (it covers payslip/statement proof, not records or retention). §5.2 also removes any further document request for small loans; the proposal adds the duty in plain words.

review_unsupported_claims: The rationale says §5.3 allows a scoring model but 'prior agreement with the NBG' is not reflected; that is accurate, but it understates the problem because the document sets a different approval route.
review_comment: §5.3 says 'მოდელი ინერგება ბანკის დირექტორატის დამტკიცების შემდეგ', which makes internal approval the only gate, against 'სავალდებულოა ... წინასწარი შეთანხმება ეროვნულ ბანკთან'. The proposal adds the NBG duty but keeps the sentence on Directorate approval, which is awkward though not contradictory.

review_unsupported_claims: The evidence cites §7.1 (internal approval by the credit committee), which only loosely relates to the duty to send procedures to the NBG; the system calls it 'partial' although nothing in the document is partly compliant. The proposal text runs the §7.1 text into the 'დანართი 1' heading, copying a parsing artefact.
review_comment: The document nowhere says that policies must be given to the NBG '10 (ათი) სამუშაო დღით ადრე' before use; §7.1 deals only with internal approval and the 2-year review. So the gap is real, but it is 'none', not 'partial'.

review_unsupported_claims: The obligation drops the 'სულ მცირე' list and reduces it to one item (borrower-definition criteria). The 'missing' text invents examples ('ასაკი, მოქალაქეობა') that the regulation does not require, and the proposal copies them. The regulation's term is 'მსესხებელთა (მათ შორის, საოჯახო მეურნეობა) განსაზღვრის კრიტერიუმები', which the policy partly handles.
review_comment: §2.3 and §3.1 cover household treatment for PTI, and the policy does set income proof (§5), restructuring (§3.4) and PTI/LTV references (§4.1), but it has no criteria on loan purpose types or on how borrowers are defined. 'Partial' fits, but demanding age and citizenship goes beyond the regulation's text, so the proposal invents requirements.

review_unsupported_claims: The obligation turns a supervisory power of the NBG (art8/p1 lead-in: 'ეროვნული ბანკი უფლებამოსილია') into a duty of the lender. The evidence ties §6.1 to risk assessment but §6.1 says nothing relevant to GRAPE or NBG assessment. The proposal adds an invented duty on the RCD.
review_comment: The regulation reads 'ეროვნული ბანკი უფლებამოსილია: ... გაითვალისწინოს რისკების შეფასებაში', which is a power of the regulator and does not create a lender duty, so there is nothing for a bank policy to comply with. The finding should be dropped, not marked 'partial'.
